title: IMPLEMENTATION OF DDU-GKY
body_text:
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is one of the cluster of initiatives under DeenDayalAntyodayaYojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through placement-linked skilling programs. To align with evolving industry requirements and emerging employment opportunities, revised guidelines under DDU-GKY 2.0 have been rolled out from FY 2025-26 with focus on industry-led training, sustainable employment, enhanced post-placement support, upskilling and reskilling opportunities and greater flexibility in training delivery. Emerging sectors such as Electric Vehicle (EV) maintenance, renewable energy, logistics, healthcare, care economy, retail, hospitality and media & entertainment are also being prioritised. Since inception, around 18.45 lakh rural youth have been trained and about 12.35 lakh candidates have been placed under the scheme.
Training under DDU-GKY has been imparted across diverse sectors including Apparel, Automotive, Beauty & Wellness, Construction, Electronics, Healthcare, Hospitality, IT-ITES, Logistics, Retail, Telecom, Agriculture and allied sectors, among others. Placement of trained candidates is facilitated through mandatory industry partnerships, employer tie-ups, job fairs, campus placement drives, industry consultations, and engagement with Sector Skill Councils and employers. The scheme mandates placement-linked outcomes and continuous industry participation in curriculum design and training delivery. Further, the features like 20% allocation of targets to captive employers in each State/UT and the batch mode payments to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) linked to successful mandatory placement period of 6 months, have been incorporated to ensure coordination with industries.
To improve retention and sustainability of employment, DDU-GKY 2.0 emphasizes long-term employment outcomes (minimum 70% placement including maximum 20% self or gig employment for minimum of 6 months) through one year post-placement tracking and support, counselling, migration support, alumni engagement, grievance redressal mechanisms, and opportunities for upskilling/reskilling. Under the revised framework, candidates are required to be tracked and supported for a longer duration to facilitate sustained employment and career progression. Since inception, about 12.35 lakh candidates have been placed under the Scheme.
For FY 2026-27, Budget Estimates (BE) of ₹ 750 crore has been kept for training around 1.37 lakh rural youth. Further, Mother Sanction amounting ₹ 361.96 crore has been issued to the States/UTs and an expenditure of ₹ 50.89 crore has been made by the States/UTs till date.
In the State of Madhya Pradesh, DDU-GKY is being implemented through the Madhya Pradesh State Rural Livelihoods Mission (MPSRLM). Since inception, around 93 thousand candidates have been trained and around 56 thousand candidates have been placed in the State of Madhya Pradesh under the scheme. Further, for FY 2026-27, mother sanction amounting to ₹ 10.00 crore has been issued to the State of Madhya Pradesh.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Rural Development informed Lok Sabha that DDU-GKY, a placement-linked skilling scheme under DAY-NRLM, has trained about 18.45 lakh and placed about 12.35 lakh rural youth since inception. Revised guidelines (DDU-GKY 2.0) rolled out from FY 2025-26 emphasize industry-led training, emerging sectors like EV maintenance and renewable energy, and long-term employment outcomes with a minimum 70% placement rate and one-year post-placement tracking. For FY 2026-27, ₹750 crore has been budgeted to train 1.37 lakh youth, with state-wise data shared for Madhya Pradesh and Gwalior Lok Sabha constituency.
enrichment.context:
DDU-GKY (Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana), launched in 2014, is a flagship placement-linked skill development programme under the Ministry of Rural Development's DAY-NRLM umbrella, targeting rural youth aged 15-35 from poor households to reduce poverty through skilling and wage/self-employment. It is part of India's broader skill development ecosystem alongside PMKVY and the National Skills Qualification Framework, and complements NRLM's focus on women's self-help groups by addressing youth employability specifically.

The revised DDU-GKY 2.0 framework reflects a policy shift towards demand-driven, sustainable employment rather than mere training completion, incorporating features like captive employer partnerships, batch-linked payments to Project Implementing Agencies tied to 6-month retention, and post-placement support mechanisms including migration assistance and grievance redressal. This addresses long-standing criticism of skill missions for low retention rates and placement quality. The prioritization of emerging sectors like EV maintenance, renewable energy, and the care economy aligns with India's green transition and demographic shifts, making this relevant to discussions on skilling, employment generation, and rural transformation.

prelims_questions.question: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is implemented as a component of which of the following?
options: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that DDU-GKY is one of the cluster of initiatives under DAY-NRLM aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction.

prelims_questions.question: As per the revised DDU-GKY 2.0 guidelines, what is the minimum placement requirement, including self/gig employment, that Project Implementing Agencies must achieve?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies DDU-GKY 2.0 emphasizes long-term employment outcomes with a minimum 70% placement including a maximum 20% self or gig employment for at least 6 months.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the objectives and features of DDU-GKY as a placement-linked skill development programme. How do the revised DDU-GKY 2.0 guidelines address the challenges of employment sustainability and industry alignment faced by earlier skilling missions in India?

Rural youth skilling programmes often face a mismatch between training imparted and actual employment generated. Critically examine the mechanisms built into DDU-GKY 2.0, such as post-placement tracking, captive employer allocation, and outcome-linked payments, to bridge this gap.
